name: Genmab A/S
moat_justification: Proven, repeatable antibody platforms (DuoBody, DuoHexaBody, HexaBody) that have produced eight approved medicines and a high-margin royalty engine (Darzalex via J&J, Kesimpta via Novartis) plus a growing owned late-stage pipeline (Epkinly, Rina-S, petosemtamab) — but the royalty stream is concentrated in Darzalex, commercialization of the biggest earners is controlled by partners, exclusivity erodes around the turn of the decade, and the $8.0B debt-funded Merus deal makes the next leg depend on a Phase 3 asset not yet approved.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

FX_CONVERTED: reporting currency DKK converted to USD at period-end ECB reference rates (frankfurter.app) — flow facts use the period-end rate, not a period average; the rates used are recorded in dcf_numbers.json fx_conversion
USD_TRANSLATIONS_USED: the issuer files its own USD convenience translations alongside its reporting currency; the engine used the filed USD figures

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 20-F filer — per-share figures scaled x0.1 ordinary shares per ADS (Genmab A/S Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2023 (SEC filing, CIK 1434265), cover — securities registered pursuant to Section 12(b): 'American Depositary Shares, each representing one-tenth of one ordinary share', trading symbol GMAB, The NASDAQ Stock Market LLC (the same class title appears on the FY2021 20-F cover)) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 5.2x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 36.9x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: Quality antibody-platform franchise, moat 6/10 — does not clear 15% at $38.15: weighted IRR 11.1%, weighted IV@15% $24.49 on the ADS-corrected median base ($1.54/ADS); clears 15% only below ~$24.49. The pre-ADS preliminary Tier S was a units artifact (per-ordinary-share OE vs per-ADS price).
moat_for: Proprietary antibody platforms (DuoBody bispecifics, DuoHexaBody, HexaBody, ADC formats) with a 25-year record of producing approved medicines — eight approved antibody medicines to date
High-margin royalty engine: Darzalex (J&J) and Kesimpta (Novartis) royalties were $1,708M of $2,051M H1 2026 revenue; Darzalex net sales $8,171M in H1 2026 (+21% YoY)
Owned late-stage pipeline diversifying beyond royalties: Epkinly net sales +48% in H1 2026, Rina-S (ProfoundBio), petosemtamab (Merus) in Phase 3 with two FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designations
Asset-light OE conversion: FY2025 capex $37M against OCF $1,186M (financials_history.csv) — royalties and product sales need almost no reinvestment
moat_against: Royalty concentration: Darzalex is the dominant royalty source and its exclusivity erodes around the turn of the decade; multiple myeloma competition (bispecifics, CAR-T) is intensifying
Partner dependence: J&J, Novartis and AbbVie control commercialization of the largest earners — Genmab collects royalties but does not control pricing, promotion or lifecycle strategy
Binary pipeline risk now levered: petosemtamab was bought for $8.0B before its Phase 3 readouts; a failure hits both the pipeline story and a balance sheet carrying ~$5.5B of new deal debt
New leverage: net debt $3,559M at FY2025 (engine) vs a historically net-cash balance sheet; interest drag and a sub-3x deleveraging commitment constrain flexibility
